subtopics.title: The Law of Universal Gravitation and Its Equation

questions.question: Newton's law of universal gravitation states that the force between two particles is:
options: Proportional to the product of the masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between their centres
Proportional to the sum of the masses and inversely proportional to the distance
Proportional to the product of the masses and inversely proportional to the distance between their surfaces
Constant for all pairs of objects

questions.question: The gravitational force between a 60 kg and an 80 kg learner sitting 1 m apart is approximately:
The distance d in the gravitation formula is measured between:
options: The nearest surfaces of the two objects
The centres of the two objects
The furthest surfaces of the two objects
Any two convenient points

questions.question: The Earth pulls a learner down with a force of 600 N. The force the learner exerts on the Earth is:
options: Zero, because the learner is too small to pull a planet
Much smaller than 600 N, in proportion to the masses
Much larger than 600 N
Exactly 600 N, directed upward on the Earth

questions.question: If the distance between two objects is doubled, the gravitational force between them becomes:
options: Half of the original force
A quarter of the original force
Double the original force
Unchanged

questions.question: If BOTH masses are doubled while the distance stays the same, the force becomes:
options: Four times larger
Twice as large
A quarter of the original
Eight times larger

questions.question: The force between two spheres is F. One mass is tripled and the distance is halved. The new force is:
options: 6F

questions.question: The force between two spheres is 3,6 × 10⁻⁷ N. When the centre-to-centre distance is doubled, the force becomes:

subtopics.title: Gravitational Acceleration from g Equals G M Over r Squared

questions.question: In deriving g = GM/r², the mass of the falling object cancels out. This explains why:
options: Heavier objects fall faster than lighter ones
All objects at the same location fall with the same acceleration
Gravity does not act on very light objects
The value of g is the same on every planet

questions.question: Using M = 7,35 × 10²² kg and r = 1,74 × 10⁶ m, the gravitational acceleration on the Moon's surface is approximately:
A satellite orbits at a height of one Earth radius ABOVE the surface. The gravitational acceleration at that height is:
options: 9,8 ÷ 4 = 2,45 m·s⁻², because it is two Earth radii from the centre
9,8 ÷ 2 = 4,9 m·s⁻², because the distance has doubled
Zero, because the satellite is in space
9,8 m·s⁻², because g never changes

questions.question: The value of g on a planet's surface depends on:
options: The mass of the object being dropped
Only the radius of the planet
The speed at which the object is released
The planet's mass and the planet's radius

subtopics.title: Weight on Other Planets and True Weightlessness

questions.question: A 70 kg astronaut travels from Earth to the Moon. Which statement is correct?
options: Her mass and weight both decrease
Her mass stays 70 kg but her weight decreases to about 113,4 N
Her mass decreases but her weight stays 686 N
Her mass and weight both stay the same

questions.question: On Mars, where g is about 3,7 m·s⁻², the weight of a 70 kg astronaut is about:
Astronauts on the space station float because:
options: Gravity at that height is zero
The station's walls shield them from gravity
Their mass becomes zero in orbit
They and the station are in continuous free fall around the Earth, so nothing supports them

questions.question: Which pairing of quantity and unit is correct?
options: Mass in kilograms; weight in newtons
Mass in newtons; weight in kilograms
Mass in kilograms; weight in kilograms
Mass in newtons; weight in newtons

questions.question: You never feel the gravitational pull of your desk because:
options: Desks are not massive enough to exert gravity
Gravity only acts downwards
Gravity between everyday objects is real but far too small to notice
Friction cancels the pull exactly

questions.question: You pull the Earth upward with 686 N, yet the Earth does not visibly move because:
options: The same force on an enormous mass produces an immeasurably small acceleration
The Earth's pull on you is much stronger than yours on it
The ground absorbs the force
The force only acts while you are jumping

questions.question: The two things that decide the size of the gravitational pull between two objects are:
options: Their speeds and their sizes
Their masses and the distance between them
Their weights and their temperatures
Their volumes and their densities

subtopics.title: Double the Distance, Quarter the Pull

questions.question: The torch-on-a-wall picture illustrates that gravity:
options: Travels at the speed of light
Only works in the dark
Gets stronger with distance
Spreads out so that doubling the distance quarters the strength

questions.question: Triple the distance between two objects and the gravitational pull becomes:
options: A third of the original
A sixth of the original
A ninth of the original
Three times the original

questions.question: Triple one mass and double the distance. The new force is:
options: Three quarters of the original force
Half of the original force
Three halves of the original force
Twelve times the original force

questions.question: Which rule must you never forget in these questions?
options: Mass changes are squared
Distance changes are always squared
Both mass and distance changes are squared
Nothing is ever squared

questions.question: A scale calibrated on Earth reads about 12 kg for a 70 kg person on the Moon because:
options: The person's body loses matter during the journey
The Moon's atmosphere presses down less
The Moon pulls each kilogram with only about 1,62 N instead of 9,8 N
Scales do not work on the Moon

questions.question: Which quantity is the same everywhere in the universe for a given object?
options: Its weight
Its mass
Its scale reading
Its gravitational acceleration

questions.question: The statement "there is no gravity in space" is wrong because:
options: Gravity at the space station's height is still nearly as strong as on the surface — astronauts float because they are in free fall
Gravity in space is actually stronger than on Earth
Astronauts are held down by magnetic boots
Space is completely empty of mass

questions.question: The flicker of weightlessness you feel just after a trampoline bounce happens because:
options: Gravity briefly switches off at the top
Your mass momentarily decreases
The trampoline pushes you upward the whole time
Nothing is supporting you — you are briefly in free fall while gravity still acts
